$meta.artifact: N.E.R.D. — AppSheet Products table: structure + content snapshot
$meta.purpose: Phase 1 prepopulation source and Phase 2 UI wiring reference. Documents the AppSheet Products table schema and its visible content as of the export date.

inputs.covers: platforms only, plus column type/order/color evidence

$meta.truncation_meaning: A '…' element at the end of a platforms array means the chip list ran to the column boundary in the screenshot; additional values may exist beyond what was visible. It is NOT a data value.
$meta.row_order: CSV export order (alphabetical by product_name). The screenshot is sorted by priority and does NOT match csv_row.
known_gaps: The AppSheet row key (UNIQUEID) for Products is not present in either input. Child references in acr_ids / resource_ids / support_ids point outward, but nothing points back in, so a Products key must be obtained before any join or round-trip write.
platforms is absent from the CSV export entirely and was transcribed from the screenshot. It requires a verified re-export before being treated as authoritative.
Enum value lists for priority, status, and platforms are observed-from-data, not read from AppSheet column configuration. Unused values may exist.
Column types below are inferred from value shape and UI affordances, not read from the AppSheet column editor.

schema.estimated_row_key: unknown — not exported; product_name is unique across all 101 rows but is a label, not a confirmed key

columns.name: product_name
columns.notes: Unique across all rows. Likely the display label; may or may not be the key.

columns.name: vendor_id
columns.notes: Stores a vendor NAME, not an opaque ID. Contains two sentinel strings that are not real vendors: 'NULL' (26 rows) and 'CANDIDATE' (11 rows). 37% of rows therefore carry no genuine vendor reference. UI shows a ref-arrow icon on this column.

columns.name: product_description
columns.notes: Max observed 420 chars — could be Text rather than LongText.

columns.name: platforms
columns.notes: NOT PRESENT IN THE CSV EXPORT. Transcribed from the screenshot. Only 22 of 101 rows have visible values; the remaining 79 are recorded as empty arrays, which may reflect genuine emptiness or export/visibility limits. Re-export before trusting.

columns.name: notes
columns.notes: Free-form editorial notes, contains embedded newlines and initialed sign-offs (e.g. '-RC'). Max observed 780 chars.

columns.name: status
columns.notes: 11 rows have no status. UI renders each value as a colored chip — colors above are observed from the screenshot and should drive the dashboard's status treatment, with a non-color cue added alongside (WCAG 1.4.1).

columns.name: last_updated
columns.notes: Stored as US-locale string 'M/D/YYYY h:mm:ss AM/PM'. All 101 values parse cleanly. Exposed here as both last_updated_raw (verbatim) and last_updated_iso (derived, for sorting).

columns.name: ncademi_product_url
columns.notes: Populated only for products already live on ncademi.org — 54 of 101. Correlates with status but is not derivable from it.

columns.name: gatherer
columns.notes: CSV stores an email address; the UI displays a person's full name, which indicates a Ref to a people table with a display-name label. Only 2 distinct values present, too few to infer the full vocabulary.

columns.name: reviewer
columns.notes: Same shape and caveats as gatherer.

columns.name: acr_ids
columns.notes: Comma-space delimited 22-character AppSheet UNIQUEID keys. 79 references across 59 rows, 0-5 per row, all distinct — strict one-to-many, no shared child rows.

columns.name: resource_ids
columns.notes: 281 references across 80 rows, 0-13 per row, all distinct. This is the highest-cardinality child relation and the one that maps onto ListingData.vendor_resources / other_resources — the Resources table must be inspected for a column that distinguishes the two.

columns.name: support_ids
columns.notes: 85 references across 61 rows, 0-3 per row, all distinct.

nerd_mapping.note: The AppSheet Products table is an editorial workflow record, not a published-listing record. It overlaps ListingData on product identity and child collections but diverges on workflow fields, which have no ListingData equivalent. Treat this as a distinct model rather than forcing it into ListingData.

maps_to_listing_data.resource_ids: vendor_resources + other_resources (via Resources table; split rule unknown)

Canvas is a learning management system (LMS) developed by Instructure that provides educators and students with tools for course management, online learning, and collaboration.

Encyclopedia Britanica is an online encyclopedia that provides reference content across a wide range of subjects.
Epic is a subscription-based digital reading platform that provides children (typically ages 12 and under) access to a large library of eBooks, audiobooks, read-to-me titles, and educational videos.

Gimkit is a game-based learning platform that allows educators and students to create and play interactive quiz-style games, using gamification features like live gameplay, in-game rewards, and real-time feedback.

Grammarly is a cloud-based AI writing assistant that reviews text for spelling, grammar, clarity, tone, and style while offering suggestions and editing support across websites, apps, and documents.
History.com provides educational content on historical events, figures, and topics through articles, videos, and interactive resources, supporting learning in history and social studies.

i-Ready Classroom Mathematics is a K–8 mathematics curriculum from Curriculum Associates that provides teacher-led lessons, digital activities, and assessments to support standards-aligned math instruction and help students develop conceptual understanding and problem-solving skills.

rows.notes:
The original product name was iReady, but the link goes to a specific diagnostic piece of the iReady system called "iReady Inform." iReady encompasses curriculum as well as diagnostics, so I wasn't sure whether this needed to be expanded or split into several products under the iReady umbrella.

From RC: I'll look into their products. I think it may make sense to split them up since there are so many, but I need to do some research.

rows.product_description: Nearpod is an instructional platform that allows educators to create and deliver interactive lessons incorporating presentations, multimedia content, and formative assessments in diverse learning environments.
PBS is a public broadcasting network that provides educational television programming, digital media content, and classroom resources for children, students, and educators.

PhET Interactive Simulations at the University of Colorado Boulder provides free interactive math and science simulations. The simulations allow students to explore concepts through visual models and experimentation and are commonly used to support inquiry-based learning.
Prodigy Game offers an interactive platform for learning mathematics and English targeted toward elementary and middle school students.
Quizlet is an online study platform that enables users to create and access digital flashcards, practice quizzes, and learning activities across a range of academic subjects.

i-Ready Inform is an online adaptive assessment that measures students’ reading and mathematics skills to identify learning needs and provide educators with data to guide instruction.

Brainly is a peer learning platform that enables students to ask and answer academic questions across subjects. It is used by students to get homework help and explanations from a community of users.

BrainPOP is an educational technology platform offering animated movies, interactive quizzes, and activities across various subjects for students in grades K-8. It focuses on making complex topics engaging and accessible through multimedia content and supporting diverse learning styles.

BrainPOP ELL is an interactive language learning platform that provides English language learners with engaging content, including animated movies, games, quizzes, and interactive features, to develop their listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. The platform supports skill development through conversational English modeled by characters and integrates vocabulary, language, and content lessons.

BrainPOP Jr. is an educational platform offering animated movies, interactive quizzes, games, and activities across various subjects for students in kindergarten through third grade. It aims to make learning engaging and accessible by providing content through multiple modalities, fostering curiosity, and supporting diverse learning styles.

Canvas Studio is a video learning platform integrated with Canvas LMS that allows educators to create, manage, and share instructional videos while embedding quizzes, discussions, and analytics to support interactive learning.

CK-12 Foundation provides a comprehensive platform offering free online textbooks (FlexBooks), videos, adaptive practice, simulations, and real-world applications for K-12 students. CommonLit is a literacy curriculum and reading comprehension platform that provides reading lessons, texts, and assessments for ELA instruction in grades 6–12. It is used in classroom and independent reading activities.

a collection of problem-solving tasks that help K–5 students build their math confidence through engaging challenges.

rows.product_description: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application that allows users to organize data, perform calculations, create charts, and analyze information using formulas and functions.

Formative is a real-time instructional and assessment platform designed for K-12 educators. It allows teachers to create digital lessons and assessments, monitor student work live as it happens, and provide immediate feedback.

Gizmos is a STEM simulation library that provides interactive simulations and inquiry-based lessons in science and mathematics topics such as biology, chemistry, physics, Earth science, algebra, and geometry. Google Forms is a web-based application that allows users to create surveys, quizzes, questionnaires, and other forms to collect information. It is part of the Google Docs Editors suite and is designed to be usable across various devices and for users of assistive technologies.
Google Sheets is a web-based spreadsheet application that allows users to organize, calculate, analyze, and collaboratively edit data in real time.
Google Slides is a web-based presentation application that enables users to create, edit, format, and collaboratively present slide decks online.

rows.notes: GJ: I'm kind of at a loss with Houghton Mifflin Harcourt. They are a publisher, which to me equates to a Vendor. They have a "Products" page, that when the link is not broken, just returns a listing of books filtered by a keyword. They certainly have digital "add-ons" to their publications, but I didn't see any evidence of an actual digital platform. An AI search for any VPAT associated with HMH returned 0 results. My recommendation is to add them as a Vendor only.

Number Corner is a skill-building program revolving around the classroom calendar.

rows.product_description: PebbleGo is a digital learning platform designed for K-5 students, offering nonfiction articles, eBooks, and teaching resources to support literacy skills and build knowledge in subjects like science and social studies. It features read-aloud audio, rich vocabulary support, and multimodal learning tools.

PebbleGo Create is a content creation tool that allows elementary students to create multimedia projects that demonstrate their learning. It provides a space for students to develop and share projects using text, images, audio, and other media elements.

Seesaw Elementary LMS is a learning management system that enables students to create and share classwork and allows teachers to assign, review, and communicate about learning activities in elementary classrooms.

Book Creator is an intuitive EdTech platform designed to empower students and teachers to create and publish interactive digital books incorporating text, images, audio, and video.
